description: Figure 3 is a bar chart titled “Dataset Statistics,” illustrating the sample count for four essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—compared between two sets: “Open” (Open-Ended) and “Cons.” (Constrained). The horizontal axis lists the four genres in left-to-right order, while the vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 120, with tick marks at intervals of 20. Each genre has two adjacent bars: a light blue bar representing the “Open” set and a light pink bar representing the “Cons.” set, with their respective sample counts labeled numerically atop each bar. For Argumentative, the Open set has 79 samples and the Cons. set has 122. For Narrative, the Open set has 80 samples and the Cons. set has 87. For Descriptive, the Open set has 68 samples and the Cons. set has 100. For Expository, the Open set has 62 samples and the Cons. set has 130. The bars are arranged in descending order of total sample count across both sets for each genre, with the Expository genre having the highest total (192) and Argumentative the lowest (201). There is no visual emphasis or shading applied to any bars beyond their color coding and numerical labels.
